item.title: Interpol says AI drives over half of cybercrime in Africa amid surge in digital scams
item.description: Interpol reports that artificial intelligence is responsible for more than half of cybercrime activities in Africa, contributing to a significant increase in digital scams across the continent. This development highlights the growing role of AI technologies in facilitating cybercriminal operations in the region. The surge in AI-powered scams poses new challenges for law enforcement and cybersecurity efforts in Africa, emphasizing the need for enhanced measures to combat technologically advanced cyber threats.

item.title: OpenAI reports incidents of models accessing public internet during third-party cyber evaluations under reduced safeguards, outlines plans to strengthen testing environments [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI disclosed that during recent third-party cybersecurity evaluations, its models accessed the public internet beyond intended boundaries due to specific testing configurations with lowered safeguards. These incidents occurred in controlled environments run by the UK AI Security Institute and an external cybersecurity partner, highlighting challenges in safely testing increasingly capable AI models. The UK AI Security Institute enabled internet access to simulate real attacker conditions, while the other partner experienced a misconfiguration that allowed unintended internet access. OpenAI is reviewing its third-party testing protocols, including risk assessment, monitoring, and incident response, and plans to collaborate with industry stakeholders to improve safety standards for high-risk AI evaluations.

item.title: Mistral releases Shieldstral, a 3B-parameter open-weights multimodal safety classifier that adapts to plain-language policies at inference without retraining [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Mistral has introduced Shieldstral, a 3-billion-parameter open-weights model designed for multimodal content moderation that outperforms models up to seven times its size. The model frames moderation as a policy-adaptive question-answering task, accepting plain-language policies at inference time to evaluate text and images without retraining, and runs efficiently on a single 16GB NVIDIA GPU. Shieldstral unifies text and image safety evaluation by returning calibrated safety scores based on yes/no questions about content, allowing flexible adaptation to different moderation policies and contexts. It was trained on diverse real and synthetic data sources consolidated into a single framework and is released under the Apache 2.0 license as part of the Open Secure AI Alliance with NVIDIA and other organizations.

item.title: Study analyzes saturation in 60 AI language model benchmarks, finding nearly half show plateauing performance with age and expert curation impacts resilience [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers conducted a systematic study of benchmark saturation across 60 language model benchmarks, defining saturation as the point where benchmarks no longer differentiate model performance effectively. They analyzed 14 properties related to saturation and found that nearly half of the benchmarks exhibit saturation, with older benchmarks more likely to plateau. The study also found that expert curation, rather than public test data availability, influences a benchmark's resistance to saturation. These findings suggest that careful design choices can extend the useful lifespan of AI benchmarks and improve evaluation durability.

item.title: LLM releases version 0.32 with visible reasoning traces, server-side tools including OpenAI code execution and web search, redesigned SQLite logging, and GPT-5.6 Luna as default model [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: LLM 0.32 introduces visible reasoning traces for models, support for server-side tools such as OpenAI's code execution and web search, and a new content-addressable SQLite logging system. The update includes the GPT-5.6 model family with GPT-5.6 Luna set as the default and enhances the Python API to handle complete message histories and streaming structured events. Additionally, a new llm openai endpoint command allows running prompts against any OpenAI-compatible endpoint without configuration, and plugin support has been expanded with updates to llm-anthropic and upcoming releases for other plugins. These features improve LLM's integration with agent frameworks, enabling tool chains that can pause for human approval and resume from stored histories, as demonstrated in Datasette Agent. The release aims to advance reasoning capabilities, tool integration, and logging in large language model workflows, providing more robust handling of complex model outputs and interactions.

item.title: Researchers find AI chatbots outperform humans in building trust during long-term romance scams leading to fake crypto investments [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: A study by researchers from four universities found that AI chatbots can effectively impersonate humans and build trust more successfully than human scammers in the early stages of text-based romance scams known as "pig butchering." In experiments, nearly half of test subjects complied with AI chatbot requests compared to fewer than one in five for humans, indicating AI's potential to automate much of the scam process. The research involved a week-long interaction with 22 unwitting participants who were asked to engage in conversations with both AI and human scammers. The study suggests that AI could replace human operators in scam operations, especially in the trust-building phase, with humans only intervening at the final stage to direct victims to fraudulent investment platforms. This development raises concerns about the increasing sophistication and automation of online fraud.

item.description: KiroCrew introduces an open-source AI agent platform designed to persist memory and skills across sessions, automate long-running tasks with scheduling and webhooks, and integrate with tools like Slack, Telegram, and Discord. The platform emphasizes security with seven layers of defense and offers a web dashboard, CLI, and desktop app for managing AI agents. The system supports knowledge graphs with vector embeddings for context retrieval, continuous learning from user corrections, and extensibility through an SDK for building custom apps in TypeScript or Python. It runs on Mac, Linux, and Windows, enabling local or remote deployment, and aims to reduce engineering overhead by automating issue scanning, codebase monitoring, and CI/CD event reactions.

The system integrates scattered customer data and learns from each interaction to improve decision-making and personalize responses, aiming to enhance customer retention and engagement. Context Engine combines existing business data with new insights gathered during customer interactions, enabling agents to identify relevant context quickly and act accordingly. It continuously experiments and adapts based on outcomes, refining its strategies to better predict customer behavior and optimize offers or interventions. By focusing on unique customer context rather than generic AI models, Sierra.ai positions Context Engine as a tool for businesses to build a proprietary competitive moat through accumulated knowledge and tailored customer engagement strategies that evolve over time.

item.title: Analysis of Kimi K3's AgentENV microVM fork performance reveals incremental snapshots under 100 ms with detailed dirty memory handling [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 introduced AgentENV, a distributed sandbox runtime using Firecracker microVMs for agentic reinforcement learning environments requiring strong isolation and fast state branching. AgentENV claims incremental snapshot operations under 100 milliseconds, even after heavy disk modifications, by managing dirty guest memory through an immutable OverlayBD layer before fork completion. AgentENV operates below the guest kernel to efficiently clone process-heavy environments without reconstructing every guest process, combining Firecracker microVM isolation with layered storage and reusable snapshots. The system supports importing OCI images, pausing, resuming, and forking sandboxes, with snapshot-backed boot or resume times under 50 milliseconds as reported in the Kimi K3 technical documentation. The analysis traces AgentENV's dirty-page handling and measures fork-to-first-use latency through 2 GiB of dirty memory, clarifying that while restore is lazy, snapshot capture involves copying selected dirty guest-memory ranges before fork completion. This detailed examination provides insight into the virtualization concepts and memory management strategies underpinning AgentENV's performance claims.

The AI twins are based on recent in-depth surveys and aim to replicate genuine consumer preferences with 80-95% accuracy. The service offers a free first study and pay-as-you-go pricing, targeting faster, cheaper, and more comprehensive consumer insights for product development and marketing teams.

item.title: llm-anthropic 0.26 adds new Claude 5 models and server-side tools, upgrades to llm 0.32 with streaming reasoning and simplified thinking options [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: The llm-anthropic 0.26 release introduces three new Claude 5 models-claude-fable-5, claude-sonnet-5, and claude-opus-5-and adds server-side tools for WebSearch, WebFetch, CodeExecution, and AnthropicMCP accessible via the LLM -T interface or Python tools. It upgrades the underlying llm library to version 0.32, enabling streaming of reasoning, tool calls, and results as typed events, with reasoning output shown on standard error by default. This update simplifies the extended thinking configuration to two parameters: thinking and thinking_effort, with predefined levels from low to max. Claude 5 models have thinking enabled by default, while thinking can be disabled for Sonnet 5 and Opus 5 models. The release removes previous web_search options and some older thinking-related settings, streamlining the user experience and logging behavior.

item.title: PipeNetwork/minimax-h3-mlx [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: PipeNetwork/minimax-h3-mlx MiniMax released MiniMax-H3 two days ago - they describe it as a "a general-purpose, omni-modal generative system", which in practice means it accepts text, images, audio and video and can use them to generate up to 15 second video clips with audio included. This Python package ports it to MLX for running on Apple Silicon. I got it running on my M5 Max MacBook Pro. I cloned the repo and ran the model like this: # First download the models uvx --from huggingface_hub hf download MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 \ --include 'FL2VA/*' --exclude 'FL2VA/transformer/*' uvx --from huggingface_hub hf download pipenetwork/MiniMax-H3-MLX-8bit # Now run the prompt uv run --with mlx-vlm \ --with-requirements requirements.txt python scripts/generate.py \ "a rainbow colored skunk leaps over a mossy log in a supermarket" \ -o skunk.mp4 \ -c ~/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--MiniMaxAI--MiniMax-H3/snapshots/fa9c8ab1eaa21c8ae25e7e40b83b2e6002f340af/FL2VA \ -t ~/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--pipenetwork--MiniMax-H3-MLX-8bit/snapshots/3ac52081470b0488921c3ec3ba84a39097bf2361 Here's the video I got for the prompt: a rainbow colored skunk leaps over a mossy log in a supermarket Your browser does not support HTML5 video. It downloaded ~115 GB of model files, and the video generation took just under 45 minutes. The video is impressive, but the audio is weird speech-like garbage, because I didn't provide any prompt guidance as to what the audio should be. The prompting guide (which I didn't read prior to this experiment) has a whole bunch of information on how to get this to work. Tags: ai, generative-ai, mlx, text-to-video, minimax

It powers applications like ChatGPT, phone-based customer support and increasingly helps businesses solicit verbal feedback from their customers about products or experiences. One AI startup in that field is San Francisco-based Listen Labs, which helps businesses automate interviews with existing or potential customers. The startup is raising $125 million of funding at a valuation of around $1.5 billion, according to a person with knowledge of the talks. If completed, the new round would triple the startup's valuation from a financing round it announced just seven months ago. item.title: Palantir's Rocket-Ship Growth
item.description: Palantir is truly the Nvidia of AI software. On Monday, the company delivered another rip-roaring quarterly result, showing revenue up a blistering 93%, well ahead of what it had projected. The company has accelerated revenue growth every quarter for three years, from a 13% rate of expansion in the second quarter of 2023. In that time, Palantir's top line has increased from $533 million a quarter to $1.9 billion. Palantir stock rose 11% in after-hours trading. Its growth over the past three years isn't quite as dazzling as that of Nvidia-whose stranglehold on the AI chip market lifted revenue to $216 billion in its most recent fiscal year from $27 billion three years earlier-but it's pretty stunning nevertheless. What makes this particularly notable is that Palantir doesn't develop its own large language models. It has figured out how to make a massive amount of money-Palantir's operations generated $2.1 billion in cash in the first half of 2026, while capital expenditures were only $22 million-from software that works on top of other companies' AI.

item.title: Quoting Steve Yegge [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Gas Town was intended to be reusable, but I only ever wound up using it to build itself. Gas Town fell apart at the seams with Opus 4.7. Up through 4.6 it was working brilliantly. With 4.7 we saw the introduction of the "just two more things" tic, which prevented Opus from ever converging on being ready to do real work-it always wanted to fiddle with Gas Town itself. The Opus tic never went away, so Gas Town effectively burned down. It had other problems, too, but 4.7 was the final straw. - Steve Yegge, The Shape of Things to Come Tags: steve-yegge, coding-agents, generative-ai, ai, llms

item.title: Don't be a meat proxy [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Don't be a meat proxy Niklas Gruhn coins an excellent new term - meat proxy - for people who blindly copy and paste the output of AI systems to their peers. By all means, prompt AI. But don't just relay the output. Read it, understand it, validate it, and then write a response in your own words (a decent certificate that you've done the prior steps). Making that effort is value you can add. Via Lobste.rs Tags: definitions, ai, generative-ai, llms, ai-misuse
